text:
jess_support: ACME says after their network migration their app in vpc-0abc1234 started getting NXDOMAIN for the private service endpoint svc.acme.internal and 502s to our private API. Can someone triage?

acme_integration: we rolled a new egress proxy + NAT last night, did not touch Route53 zones. App saw DNS NXDOMAIN first, then timeouts.

jess_support: ok can you paste outputs of these quick checks from an app host: 
```
# dig against node resolver
dig @127.0.0.53 svc.acme.internal +short
# dig against VPC resolver (amazon-provided)
dig @172.31.0.2 svc.acme.internal +short
# check resolver associations
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --query 'HostedZones[?Name==`svc.acme.internal.`]'
```

acme_integration: dig against node-local returned NXDOMAIN. dig to 172.31.0.2 also NXDOMAIN. route53 show returns hosted zone but no VPC associations. output: ```{ "HostedZones": [{ "Id": "/hostedzone/Z1EXAMPLE", "Name": "svc.acme.internal.", "CallerReference": "..." }] }```

sam_eng: that strongly suggests the VPC wasn't associated with the private hosted zone after migration. Two places to check: (1) route53 VPC associations, (2) route53resolver outbound rules / forwarding rules if you use central resolver. run: `aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id Z1EXAMPLE` and `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=VPCId,Values=vpc-0abc1234`

acme_integration: ran both, no associations returned. we assumed association stayed in place during migration. also noticed our egress proxy terminates TLS and rewrites SNI/Host header for some domains to route multi-tenant traffic. could that break internal lookups?

lee_sre_oncall: two separate issues can look like this: missing VPC association -> NXDOMAIN; proxy SNI rewrite -> TLS mismatch/502 when you force IP. First fix the DNS association. Steps: 1) Associate VPC with hosted zone (console or `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z1EXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0abc1234`) 2) Flush node-local DNS caches (`kubectl exec -n kube-system ds/node-local-dns -c node-local-dns -- pkill -HUP nodelocal`) or restart pod. 3) If you have a central resolver, ensure a rule exists to forward that zone or VPC is in the correct outbound resolver config.

acme_integration: associated the VPC via CLI just now (used the aws command). waiting a minute then: dig @172.31.0.2 svc.acme.internal +short -> `10.0.5.12`. node-local still showed NXDOMAIN until we restarted the node-local-dns daemonset. after restart node-local returns 10.0.5.12.

jess_support: progress. can you also test curl to confirm TLS/Host handling? run: `curl -v --resolve svc.acme.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://svc.acme.internal/` (this forces IP and SNI Host).

acme_integration: did that, earlier it returned a 502 and curl verbose showed TLS cert CN = api.redwood.com (proxy replaced SNI). After we changed proxy passthrough rule for `svc.acme.internal` to preserve client SNI, curl returns 200.

sam_eng: summary / root cause: during migration VPC lost association with private hosted zone -> NXDOMAIN. Additionally, egress proxy was configured to terminate TLS and rewrite SNI for multi-tenant routing which caused cert mismatch when hitting the service by IP. Both needed fixes.

jess_support: thanks all. action items: acme_integration will add VPC association to infra checklist for migrations, update proxy allowlist to passthrough SNI for internal svc hostnames. sam_eng/lee_sre_oncall will draft a short KB and add a runbook entry on verifying hosted zone associations post-migration. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Support ticket created SUP-12345: https://redwood.support/SUP-12345 (linked to this thread).

jess_support: closing thread, will follow up in KB doc and link into onboarding playbook.
